newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Volunteers burying "tens of bodies" in east Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Volunteers burying "tens of bodies" in east Zaire.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Wednesday local volunteers in the east Zairean town of Bukavu were burying bodies after recent fighting to lessen the threat of disease.

"Zairean Red Cross volunteers in Bukavu are busy burying tens of bodies to avoid epidemics. We don't have an exact number on the number of corpses -- 20-30 or more," spokesman Rolin Wavre of the Geneva-based agency said.

The ICRC had no details because its staff and other aid agencies pulled out of Bukavu at the weekend because of lack of security. An estimated half a million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees in the region are fleeing fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels.
The picturesque town of Bukavu faces Rwanda's border town of Cyangugu across lake Kivu.
The border area is extremely tense after two days of gunfire between Rwandan and Zairean forces and a Rwandan military sortie into Zairean territory.

On Wednesday, Rwanda's Rwandan Vice-President and Defence Minister Paul Kagame told a news conference in his capital Kigali that Rwanda would be forced to respond if faced with what he called Zairean aggression.
In Geneva, U.N. refugee agency spokesman Fernando del Mundo said Rwandan villagers living near the border were evacuating their children to a school away from the frontier.
Deadly rivalry between ethnic Hutus and Tutsis, which resulted in nearly one million dead in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, has spilled into Zaire, which is host to 1.1 million Rwandan refugees.
